sense: of a law or a text

terms.gloss: a section or head of a law or a writing; a chapter
evidence: Traupman 273 (a clause in a law or a treaty)
M-O s.v. parts: chapter (division of book)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “in writings, a division, section, paragraph, chapter”; ā prīmō capite lēgis usque ad extrēmum (Cic. Agr. 2.15).

evidence: Cic. Fin. 1.7: locōs quōsdam trānsferam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In this sense the plural is locī, not loca (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a clause; the article of a treaty
terms.comment: The jurists’ word for a short clause; the articles of treaties and concordats in later Latin (Morgan–Owens).

phrases.english: I have appended the sections of the law to this letter.

phrases.latin: at tūte scrīpsistī ad mē quoddam caput lēgis Clōdium in cūriae poste fīxisse, nē referrī nēve dīcī licēret
phrases.english: but you wrote to me yourself that Clodius had nailed a section of the law to the doorpost of the senate house, forbidding the matter to be raised or spoken of

sources: Lewis & Short: caput · Lewis & Short: locus · Lewis & Short: articulus
